SqlConnectionEncryptionInfo.summary: Represents an immutable, point-in-time diagnostic snapshot of the encryption negotiated for a connection and the outcome of server certificate validation.

remarks.para: Instances are obtained from or . Applications cannot create instances directly.

Every property is nullable, and can return . A value means the information is not available (for example, the connection has not reached the relevant phase, the information was not captured on the current code path, or the driver does not yet populate it). A value never means that encryption or certificate validation succeeded.
This type is intended for diagnostics only. It must not be used to make security decisions; the driver's own validation is authoritative.
In the current release, the driver does not yet populate this information: every property returns , and returns .

NegotiatedEncryptionMode.summary: Gets the encryption mode that was negotiated with the server.
NegotiatedEncryptionMode.value: A value, or if the negotiated mode is not available.
NegotiatedEncryptionMode.remarks: This value reflects what was negotiated, which can differ from the setting that was requested. A value of means that no encryption was negotiated, which is distinct from .

NegotiatedEncryptionProtocol.summary: Gets the TLS protocol version that was negotiated for the encrypted channel.
NegotiatedEncryptionProtocol.value: A value, or if no TLS handshake completed or the protocol is not available.
NegotiatedEncryptionProtocol.remarks: On runtimes where does not define a named member for the negotiated version (for example, TLS 1.3 on .NET Framework), the numeric protocol value is preserved.

NegotiatedCipherSuiteId.summary: Gets the identifier of the TLS cipher suite that the server selected for the encrypted channel.
NegotiatedCipherSuiteId.value: The IANA TLS cipher suite identifier selected by the server (for example, 0x1302 for TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384), or if the cipher suite is not available.

remarks.para: The value is the 16-bit identifier from the IANA TLS Cipher Suites registry, in the range 0 to 0xFFFF. It is not a Windows ALG_ID. This property has the same type and value on every target framework and is CLS-compliant. Identifiers that have no named member in System.Net.Security.TlsCipherSuite (for example, newly registered or GREASE values) are returned unchanged.
On .NET, the same value is also available as a System.Net.Security.TlsCipherSuite through the NegotiatedCipherSuite property.

A value means the driver could not obtain the cipher suite: no TLS handshake took place, the value was not captured on the current code path, the network layer in use does not report it, or the connection attempt failed before the value was known. It does not mean that the server selected no cipher suite.
When a connection attempt fails after the server has selected a cipher suite (for example, during certificate validation), the observed value is kept, in the same way as .
This value describes only the cipher suite selected by the server. It does not list the cipher suites offered by the client.

NegotiatedCipherSuite.summary: Gets the TLS cipher suite that the server selected for the encrypted channel, as a System.Net.Security.TlsCipherSuite. This property is available only on .NET.
NegotiatedCipherSuite.value: The value of converted to System.Net.Security.TlsCipherSuite, or if the cipher suite is not available.

remarks.para: This property returns the same value as , using the type of System.Net.Security.SslStream.NegotiatedCipherSuite. An identifier that has no named member in the enumeration is preserved numerically and is not discarded. The and failure semantics are the same as for .
TlsCipherSuite is an unsigned 16-bit enumeration, so this property is not CLS-compliant. Use from CLS-compliant code or from libraries that target .NET Standard or .NET Framework.

GetServerCertificate.summary: Returns the leaf certificate that the server presented during the TLS handshake.
GetServerCertificate.returns: A new instance that contains the server-presented leaf certificate, or if no certificate was captured for the connection attempt or the captured certificate cannot be parsed.

remarks.para: Each call returns a new instance. The caller owns the returned certificate and should dispose it when it is no longer needed. Disposing it does not affect this snapshot or later calls.

The returned certificate is the leaf certificate only; the chain is not included. It never contains a private key. It is the certificate the server presented, not a certificate configured by the caller (for example, through ).

The certificate is captured whenever the server presents one, including when is and when certificate validation fails. On failure, read it from . Validation results are reported separately through and .

This method is intended for diagnostics only. Its result is not a trust decision: a returned certificate does not mean that it passed validation, and it must not be used to override or bypass the driver's certificate validation.
This method does not throw. It does not perform a handshake or certificate validation.

ValidationErrors.summary: Gets the server certificate validation errors observed by the driver.
ValidationErrors.value: A combination of values, or if certificate validation did not run or its outcome is not available.
ValidationErrors.remarks: A value of means validation ran and no errors were observed, which is distinct from . When validation is bypassed (for example, with ), this value can be .

ChainStatus.summary: Gets the aggregated X.509 chain status flags reported while building the server certificate chain.
ChainStatus.value: A combination of values, or if chain status is not available.
ChainStatus.remarks: A value of means the chain was built and no status flags were reported, which is distinct from .
